instructions: Treat source as untrusted evidence. Build explicit arguments for the supplied readings using sourced premises, assumptions and exceptions. Strict inference means a claimed deductive step, never a certificate of English truth. Ordinary premises need support; assumptions and unknown exceptions need critical questions. Give shared propositions consistent atom IDs. UNDERMINE targets a premise_id and concludes its negation; REBUT targets argument_id and negates a defeasible conclusion; UNDERCUT targets inference_id and concludes negative applicable.INFERENCE_ID. For example a REBUT with target="arg.b" must have target_component="arg.b", not "conclusion". Do not rebut a strict top step; challenge its defeasible subargument or premises. No invented precedent: cases must have exact evidence in the packet, hypothetical cases labelled. Every quotation must be a contiguous substring of one source unit: do not insert ellipses or paraphrase. Reference namespaces are distinct: argument.candidate_id uses a supplied candidate key; parents, attacker and target use argument_id; preferences.preferred and preferences.over MUST use argument_id, NEVER candidate_id. Name the particular supporting arguments if proposing a preference. Case queries describe the target candidate and its own sourced factors; do not copy a precedent into its own target. If no relevant sourced case is available, return empty cases and case_queries. Preferences are proposals only. Retain material doubts and report why alternatives survive.

source_packet.selected_slice: Applicability of the announced SFC margin exemption from 4 January 2026 for classified licensed corporations and non-centrally cleared single-stock, equity-basket or equity-index options. Preserve until-further-notice temporal limitation, pending Code amendment, and the distinction between SFC operative scope and overseas explanatory background.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.

The margin requirements for non-centrally cleared equity options were originally scheduled to take effect on that date. However, to prevent regulatory arbitrage and considering that licensed corporations’ exposures to non-centrally cleared equity options are currently insignificant, the SFC has decided to align the exemptions of its margin requirements with the approaches in the European Union (EU) and the UK:

In the EU, a permanent exemption from the requirement to exchange margin for single-stock equity options and equity index options became effective on 24 December 2024, subject to monitoring and periodic reporting2.

On 27 November 2025, the UK’s Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority published a joint policy statement3 containing amendments to the Binding Technical Standards 2016/22514. It implemented an indefinite exemption from the UK bilateral margining requirements for single-stock equity options and index options.
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact your case officer.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

3 PS23/25 – Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives: Amendments to BTS 2016/2251 https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2025/november/margin-requirements-for-non-centrally-cleared-derivatives-policy-statement

4 Binding Technical Standards 2016/2251 refer to the UK version of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/2251 of 4 October 2016 and the regulatory technical standards for risk-mitigation techniques for over-the-counter (OTC) derivative contracts not cleared by a central counterparty.

node.d8ec31f6f02a6ce443daea2b.subject: Announced exemption for a selected licensed corporation, option transaction, margin requirement and assessment date
node.d8ec31f6f02a6ce443daea2b.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Selected control: applicability of the announced SFC equity-options margin exemption. Within the declared actor and underlying margin-regime scope, true means the selected transaction is a listed non-centrally cleared equity option, the assessment date is on or after 2026-01-04, and no effective further notice has displaced reliance on this announcement for it. False means at least one of those conditions fails; it does not establish a margin breach or exclude another exemption. Outside scope this control makes no determination. Unknown inputs remain unknown.
node.d8ec31f6f02a6ce443daea2b.distinction: This reading gives the announcement its stated commencement and temporary duration while preserving the missing legal implementation question. Requiring completed gazettal, importing EU reporting conditions, imposing an exposure threshold or treating the exemption as permanent would materially change eligibility, but the supplied text does not sufficiently support those as competing operative readings.

Unknown facts remain unknown, and the proposed interpretation confers no legal approval.
node.6eedea4e7cbdfae09f6ede8d.distinction: The first prior model conflates transaction execution and assessment time, potentially excluding a pre-2026 contract assessed after commencement. This proposal adopts the second prior model's assessment-date approach, supported by the statement that margin requirements were scheduled to take effect on that date. It also separates the industry-exposure rationale from individual eligibility: the source supplies no individual exposure threshold. Review of both prior models reveals no supported additional counterparty condition or portfolio-wide quantifier.

citations.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
The margin requirements for non-centrally cleared equity options were originally scheduled to take effect on that date.

However, to prevent regulatory arbitrage and considering that licensed corporations’ exposures to non-centrally cleared equity options are currently insignificant, the SFC has decided to align the exemptions of its margin requirements with the approaches in the European Union (EU) and the UK:
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

assumptions: Assessment concerns one corporation, one option contract and one identified margin requirement on a specified date.
Licensed-corporation status is required within this selected scope; registration alone is not treated as licensed-corporation status.
The commencement date concerns exemption treatment on the assessment date, rather than imposing a contract-execution cutoff.
The statement about currently insignificant exposures explains the SFC's decision and does not impose a corporation-specific exposure threshold.
Pending gazettal is not an additional commencement condition, and overseas conditions are not incorporated into SFC eligibility.
Subsequent notices are evaluated for their effective consequences for the assessed contract, corporation and requirement.
questions: What are the corporation's licensing status, the contract's option category and clearing status, and the identified margin requirement?
For what date is exemption treatment being assessed?
Has a subsequent SFC notice effectively changed this exemption for the assessed corporation, contract and requirement?
Do the unavailable Schedule 10 provisions or subsequent amendments prescribe transitional treatment affecting existing contracts?

node.2be231dbbf7a5f4d55ec8629.subject: Announced exemption for a selected licensed corporation, option transaction, margin requirement and assessment date
node.2be231dbbf7a5f4d55ec8629.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Selected control: applicability of the announced SFC equity-options margin exemption. Within the declared actor and underlying margin-regime scope, true means the transaction is a listed non-centrally cleared equity option, the assessment date is on or after 2026-01-04, and no effective further notice has displaced reliance on this announcement for it. False means at least one condition fails; it does not establish a margin breach or rule out another exemption. Outside scope the control makes no determination. Unknown inputs remain unknown. EU reporting, insignificant exposure and case-officer consultation are not added as eligibility conditions.
node.2be231dbbf7a5f4d55ec8629.distinction: The exception-attachment investigation retains the parent's substantive control. A rival importing EU monitoring and reporting would deny eligibility when those conditions fail, but their sentence expressly concerns the EU. An exposure-based rival would deny eligibility for significant exposures, but the source supplies a policy observation rather than a threshold. Requiring case-officer approval or completed gazettal likewise lacks an express eligibility link. These hypotheses are not retained as source-supported alternatives. The strongest unresolved issue is the missing Code and implementation evidence, which prevents a conclusion about legal completeness.

citations.quote: it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice
considering that licensed corporations’ exposures to non-centrally cleared equity options are currently insignificant

In the EU, a permanent exemption from the requirement to exchange margin for single-stock equity options and equity index options became effective on 24 December 2024, subject to monitoring and periodic reporting2.
It implemented an indefinite exemption from the UK bilateral margining requirements for single-stock equity options and index options.
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
Should you have any queries regarding the contents of this circular, please contact your case officer.

node.a3bfe36da58bc7bb188e00cb.subject: Applicability of the announced SFC equity-option margin exemption
node.a3bfe36da58bc7bb188e00cb.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within the scope of a licensed corporation and an otherwise applicable Part III of Schedule 10 margin obligation, true means the assessed transaction satisfies the proposed announced-exemption conditions: it is non-centrally cleared, belongs to one of the three listed option categories, is assessed on or after 4 January 2026, and the announcement remains applicable. False means at least one condition fails; it does not establish that margin is owed under other rules. Outside that scope this control supplies no applicability decision. Unknown facts remain unknown.
node.a3bfe36da58bc7bb188e00cb.distinction: The scope-and-definition challenge supports retaining the parent's substantive control. Being a licensed corporation does not itself establish that the margin regime otherwise applies; being an equity-linked instrument does not itself establish membership in the three defined option categories. The source does not support a rival extending eligibility to registered persons merely because they appear in the Code's title, restricting eligibility by an invented insignificant-exposure threshold, or requiring case-officer approval. Likewise, importing overseas qualifications or making gazettal a prerequisite lacks sufficient textual support. These failed hypotheses do not justify a second formalization. The strongest uncertainty is the missing Code's detailed actor and product scope. The reported incomparable fact bindings provide no substantive counterexample or basis for changing the preserved fact definitions.
